question: Reckoning and Resilience (2022), presented at Duke University's Nasher Museum of Art, was the first show devoted solely to artists from North Carolina since Across County Lines, held four years earlier. Those who curated the 2022 exhibition featured painters such as Renzo Ortega, photographers such as Ashley Johnson, and mixed-media creators such as Johannes Barfield. Yet while Johnson's piece would have suited the theme of Across County Lines, the pieces by Ortega and Barfield would not have. If true, which fact about the Across County Lines exhibition would most directly back up the underlined claim?
option a: It featured a larger number of artists than Reckoning and Resilience did.
option b: It was made up primarily of pieces by mixed-media artists.
option c: It was assembled specifically to highlight works not held by the Nasher Museum.
option d: It was made up entirely of pieces by photographers.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The claim marks Johnson the photographer as fitting while Ortega and Barfield do not, so an all-photography Across County Lines directly supports it.

question: Examining animals in a lab makes it possible to control variables in a systematic way, but taking animals out of their natural surroundings may alter their behavior and biology in ways that are hard to anticipate. With this in mind, biologists Rebecca M. Calisi-Rodriguez and George E. Bentley reviewed research on brown-throated three-toed sloths and canaries in order to determine whether findings from field studies matched those from laboratory studies. Consequently, evidence that brown-throated three-toed sloths generally sleep fewer than 10 hours a day in the wild would have no bearing on Calisi-Rodriguez and Bentley's inquiry if ______
option a: this sleep pattern has never been examined in a laboratory setting.
option b: comparable data have been gathered for canaries in the lab but not in the wild.
option c: the brains of male canaries undergo predictable seasonal changes in the wild.
option d: they generally sleep more than 15 hours a day in the lab.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The inquiry compares wild and lab results, so wild data with no lab counterpart would be irrelevant to it.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? ______ a US state upon ratifying the US Constitution on November 21, 1789, was consequently able, through its delegates to the US Congress, to cast a vote on whether Ohio would be admitted as a state on March 1, 1803.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A participial modifier set off by a comma correctly attaches to the subject North Carolina before the main verb "was."

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Canada's Hare dog existed before Europeans colonized the Americas but eventually disappeared as a result of crossbreeding with other kinds of dogs. The Xoloitzcuintli, by contrast, whose Mexican roots likewise predate colonization, has survived. And DNA analysis indicates that the rural Southeastern US's Carolina dog is descended in part from precolonial breeds, with European dog breeds ______ most of its ancestry.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Contributing" logically conveys that European breeds supply the bulk of the Carolina dog's ancestry.

question: Port Clarence Indian paintbrush (Castilleja caudata) is a plant native to Alaska, where historically the severe boreal climate has hindered would-be invasive species. Over the past few decades, though, bird vetch (Vicia cracca) has taken hold in Alaska. Research has indicated that progressively warmer spring temperatures favor invasive plants over native ones, yet none of that research has examined boreal ecosystems, even though comparable temperature shifts are happening there. To address this gap, biologists Christa Mulder and Katie Spellman monitored C. caudata and V. cracca, along with additional native and invasive species, across several years. If true, which finding from Mulder and Spellman's study would most directly support the claim that plant species in boreal ecosystems may not display the pattern observed in studies of plant species in other kinds of ecosystems?
option a: In years with historically typical spring temperatures, C. caudata and V. cracca generally produced leaves at roughly the same time, but in years with relatively warm springs, V. cracca produced leaves earlier than C. caudata did.
option b: Although C. caudata generally produced fewer leaves per year than V. cracca did, the year-to-year differences in spring temperatures during the study stayed within the historically typical range.
option c: Both C. caudata and V. cracca generally produced more leaves in years with relatively warm springs than in years with historically typical spring temperatures, but the increase was greater for V. cracca than for C. caudata.
option d: Although C. caudata and V. cracca generally produced their first leaves at different times, the magnitude of that difference stayed constant from year to year even though spring temperatures rose considerably between years.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A native-invasive timing gap that stays fixed despite warming shows the warm-spring advantage is absent in this boreal case.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? To grasp what scholars consider the allegorical intent of Fragonard's 18th-century painting ______ to embody the sense of excitement that pervades new relationships--a viewer must become acquainted with the painting's symbolic elements.
option a: The Progress of Love: The Meeting, namely,
option b: The Progress of Love: The Meeting--namely,
option c: The Progress of Love: The Meeting, namely
option d: The Progress of Love: The Meeting, namely--
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A dash before "namely" pairs with the later dash to enclose the explanatory aside.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The water moving through a river's hyporheic zone--that is, the underground area where surface water blends with groundwater--travels not only below the channel but also ______ it. In fact, by charting aquatic organisms found in soil beyond a waterway's banks, researchers have shown how far the hyporheic zone reaches, a distance that for a major river such as the Congo can extend up to 400 meters from the channel.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Adjacent to" fits water that spreads sideways from the channel, as the 400-meter reach shows.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Employing tracking instruments like depth loggers, Nicole Esteban and her colleagues investigated how species as unlike one another as the loggerhead turtle and the pygmy blue whale swim near the surface. Their work breaks from the bulk of depth-tracking research, which has traditionally ______ the deepest and longest dives.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Prioritized" contrasts with a study that instead focused on near-surface swimming.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? To grasp what scholars regard as the allegorical intent of Beuckelaer's 16th-century painting ______ to embody the idea of air's importance to human experience--a viewer must become acquainted with the painting's symbolic elements.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A dash before "namely" pairs with the later dash to set off the explanatory aside.

question: In The Jazz Continuum, LaTasha Barnes, Alain Lauture, and fellow dancers fluidly blend contemporary dance forms--among them hip-hop and voguing--with features of the Lindy Hop, a swing dance popular in the 1930s that originated in the Black American community of Harlem, New York. Prompted by Barnes's interest in the resemblances between the Lindy Hop and these apparently unrelated styles, the production's choreography reveals just how connected their histories really are. The show thus stands as evidence of the Lindy Hop's lasting impact on American culture. Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
option a: It explains why the historical links among the dance styles mentioned earlier in the text have generally gone unnoticed.
option b: It offers support for the text's assertion that the Lindy Hop has had a greater cultural impact than the other dances featured in The Jazz Continuum have had.
option c: It specifies the particular ways in which the Lindy Hop resembles the contemporary dance styles discussed in the text.
option d: It identifies the motivation for The Jazz Continuum's choreographic approach that is described earlier in the text.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The underlined phrase supplies the motivation behind the show's choreographic approach.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? To grasp what scholars take to be the allegorical intent of Matsys's 16th-century painting ______ to embody the tension between material wealth and spiritual principles--a viewer must become acquainted with the painting's symbolic elements.
option a: The Money Changer and His Wife--namely,
option b: The Money Changer and His Wife, namely,
option c: The Money Changer and His Wife, namely
option d: The Money Changer and His Wife, namely--
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A dash before "namely" pairs with the later dash to enclose the appositive explanation.

question: The function f(x) = 900(0.5)^(x/12) models the predicted intensity of a beam, f(x), given as the number of photons in the beam, at a depth of x millimeters below the surface of a certain material. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the statement f(12) = 450?
option a: At the surface of the material, a beam has a predicted intensity of 12 photons in the beam.
option b: At the surface of the material, a beam has a predicted intensity of 450 photons in the beam.
option c: At 12 millimeters below the surface of the material, a beam has a predicted intensity of 450 photons in the beam.
option d: At 450 millimeters below the surface of the material, a beam has a predicted intensity of 900 photons in the beam.
subject: Math
shortexplanation: f(12) = 450 means at a depth of 12 millimeters the beam's predicted intensity is 450 photons.
